version.approval_notes:
Build instructions (reproduce the uploaded package exactly):
1. Node.js 22 or newer and npm (tested with Node 22.23 and 26.13).
2. Unzip the attached sources zip and open a terminal in it.
3. npm ci
4. npm run build:firefox
5. The extension is in .output/firefox-mv3 (npm run zip:firefox writes the zip).

The code is bundled by WXT (Vite + TypeScript + React); the original sources are in src/. Public repository: https://github.com/akibh-dev/blockflow (the tag of this version).

- No remote code, no analytics, no network request of its own; requests are only those the user's workflows make.
- innerHTML linter warnings: src/dom/picker.ts and src/dom/recorder.ts set shadow.innerHTML to constant strings inside a closed shadow root; React uses innerHTML internally for its own elements. No page or user content is assigned.
- Site access is optional and requested per workflow; no host_permissions at install.
- declarativeNetRequest is required in the Firefox build because Firefox does not accept it as optional. Used only while a Route block runs: session rules limited to the workflow's tab, removed when the run ends. No access to page content; redirects still need the site access the user granted.
- nativeMessaging (optional): only when the user switches on "Allow outside control", to talk to a local helper (the blockflow-bridge npm package). Off by default.
- data_collection_permissions: none. Everything stays on the device.

To try it: click the toolbar button (the editor opens in a tab), create a workflow with Open Tab (https://example.com) -> Read Element (element: h1) -> Log (message: {{value}}), press Run and allow access to example.com. The log shows "Example Domain".
